title: Git on Your Mac
subtitle: Clone, status, commit — in Terminal
description: Part 2 of Git & GitHub — leave the website and use git locally. Teachy coaches you through Terminal using whatever's on your screen.
learningOutcomes: Open Terminal (or another shell) on your Mac
Confirm git is installed (or know how to get it)
Clone a public repository to your computer
Check status and see what changed
Make a small edit and create a local commit

goals.title: Open Terminal
goals.goal: Have a terminal window ready so you can run git commands.
goals.coachAsk: Help me open Terminal on my Mac and get to a prompt where I can type commands. Point at what I should use if I'm looking at the screen.
goals.doneWhen: A terminal or shell window is open and ready for typing.
tips: Terminal.app, iTerm, or Warp all work
You just need a command prompt

goals.title: Check that git works
goals.goal: Run a command that shows git is installed (or clearly see how to install it).
goals.coachAsk: How do I check whether git is installed on my Mac? Walk me through the command and point if something on screen helps.
goals.doneWhen: Terminal shows git version output, or the learner has started an install path and confirmed they're unblocked.
tips: macOS may prompt to install developer tools — that's okay

goals.title: Clone a repository
goals.goal: Clone a public GitHub repo onto your Mac so you have a local copy.
goals.coachAsk: Help me clone a public GitHub repository to my computer with git. I can pick any small public repo — guide me through clone and where the folder ends up.
goals.doneWhen: A clone completed successfully, or a local repo folder from the clone is visible in Terminal / Finder.
tips: Any small public repo is fine
Pick a folder you're comfortable downloading into

goals.title: Check git status
goals.goal: Inside the cloned repo, run status (or equivalent) and understand what it's telling you.
goals.coachAsk: I'm in a cloned repo — how do I check git status and what does a clean vs dirty tree mean? Help me run it.
goals.doneWhen: git status (or clear status output) has been shown in the terminal for that repo.
tips: cd into the cloned folder first
Clean usually means nothing to commit

goals.title: Make a local commit
goals.goal: Change a file, stage it, and create a local commit with a message — no push required yet.
goals.coachAsk: Help me make a tiny edit in this repo, stage it, and create a local git commit. Keep it beginner-friendly and don't push yet.
goals.doneWhen: A new local commit exists (git log / status shows the commit), or the learner confirmed they completed commit.
tips: Editing README with a typo fix is perfect
Push comes in the next course
